query: How do I bleed a radiator?
answer:
First turn the heating off and wait for the radiators to cool, because the water and air inside can be hot enough to scald you [1]. You'll need a radiator key (a flat-head screwdriver works on some valves), a cloth, and a towel or container to catch drips [1]. The bleed valve is usually at the top corner of the radiator, on the side opposite the main control valve [2]. Hold the cloth under it and turn the key anticlockwise about a quarter to half a turn. Don't open it all the way [1][2]. You'll hear air hissing out. When the hissing stops and water starts coming out steadily, close the valve firmly without overtightening it [1][2].

If several radiators need bleeding, a common tip is to start downstairs with the one farthest from the boiler [2]. If you have a sealed system, such as a combi boiler, check the boiler pressure gauge afterwards. A small drop is normal, and British Gas says about 1 to 1.5 bar is typical with the heating off. If it's too low, top up the pressure following your boiler's instructions [1]. Then turn the heating back on and check that every radiator heats evenly from top to bottom. If one keeps going cold at the top, call a heating engineer [1].
